A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SR-Reward research and contain 26 pages, including Appendices A–H. The text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original SR-Reward experiments on D4RL and ManiSkill2 in Section 4, plus ablations, sensitivity analyses, policy comparisons, and online RL results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Table 1, the negative-sampling evaluations, and the supplementary experiments in Appendices A–H.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same architecture, successor-representation norm reward, negative-sampling procedure, four loss terms, and joint training procedure. Their movement between pages does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same toy maze, four MuJoCo tasks, four Adroit tasks, and three ManiSkill2 tasks. The data-quality coverage and HalfCheetah online RL scenario in the appendices are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain identical: BC and true-reward f-DVL/SparseQL in Table 1, the VINS-style negative-sampling comparison in Figure 7, and the TD3 reward variants in Appendix H.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same training budgets, checkpoint selection using 25 evaluation rollouts, and final evaluation on 50 fresh rollouts. Model configurations, ablation settings, and return normalization in the appendices also match.

E4.justification: The negative-sampling tests, data-size and data-quality ablations, action-space policy comparison, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and online RL test are all retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and report means and standard deviations across seeds. The uncertainty displays in the figures are unchanged, with no added or removed statistical reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 and all plotted results match. For example, SparseQL with SR-Reward achieves 71.03 ± 18.41 on StackCube in both versions. The appendix results and reported qualitative findings are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and assumptions in Section 2, training equations in Section 3, and occupancy-measure derivation in Appendix C are unchanged. No proof, derivation, or formal property is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about offline reward learning, independence from the learner’s policy, negative sampling, and competitive performance. The added code-availability sentence does not revise these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain identical, including negative sampling’s local protection, difficulties with online exploration, sensitivity to suboptimal demonstrations, and the need for further theoretical justification.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository address at the end of the abstract, absent from v2. Implementation, hyperparameter, training, and normalization details otherwise remain unchanged. This establishes added access information, not verified repository contents.

R1.justification: Section 5, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. The new publication and review information concerns this paper itself and does not alter its positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 adds publication and review information, a code-availability sentence, and Section 8 acknowledging funding. The scientific prose and organization of the existing sections and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds publication headers and reflows the main text. Figure 5 moves from page 6 to 7, Algorithm 1 from page 7 to 8, and Figure 7 from page 10 to 11. Figure content, captions, axes, and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new code-repository address modestly improves reproducibility documentation by providing access information missing from v2. The scientific content, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, while the other additions are chiefly administrative. The supported benefit is limited to documentation; repository contents and usability cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
